Technical & price structure: In plain terms: the intrinsic DCF/SOTP value is ~EGP 11–12 a share. The market pays ~EGP 21 for continued 30% growth and a falling EGP rate path. That’s the bet.
Monte Carlo — where could the price go?: Below EGP 10.20 — the bear-case value, which assumes digitisation growth stalls and the EGP rate path stays adverse — the market would be pricing in worse than our most pessimistic case, the point where we’d rebuild the study.

One Monte Carlo model, 50,000 paths, driven by 10 outside forces: the EGP interest-rate path, digitisation throughput, cloud demand, competitive pressure, cost inflation, a regulatory/fee shock, new government mandates, tourism volumes, a CBE rate-cut surprise, and index flows. Full mechanics in the methodology .
FAQ: What is the fair-value range for e-finance (EFIH)? — testahil publishes a probability distribution of where EFIH could trade over the next 1–3 months — the simulated 5th–95th percentile range and the central 50% — not a single price target or a buy/sell call. The full study and open model show the methodology. This is educational analysis, not investment advice.

How is the EFIH valuation calculated? — The study uses an instrument-appropriate lens — a sum-of-the-parts / RNAV build for a real-estate developer — combined with a 50,000-path Monte Carlo simulation that expresses the result as a probability distribution. Every assumption is visible and editable in the free Excel model.

Does testahil recommend buying or selling EFIH? — No. testahil never issues buy, sell, or hold recommendations. It publishes fair-value ranges and probability distributions as educational material, and grades its own forecasts publicly when they resolve.

Is the e-finance for Digital & Financial Investments model free to download? — Yes. The full EFIH valuation study (Word/PDF) and the open Excel model are free to download, with every assumption editable.
